sources_and_data: Direct symbolic proof from the finite-tree matching-swap definitions
Aichholzer et al. ESA 2022 primary tree-hardness paper
method: Prove cut balance on every tree edge, define exact directional demand r(e), decompose actual edge use into mandatory traffic plus nonnegative slack, and derive an exact star formula for a fixed center with multiple disjoint leaf cycles. Compare the result with the published subdivided-star stretch theorem and adversarially review the LB_hub upper-bound conjecture.
mathematical_claim: For every tree edge e under a one-token-per-vertex permutation, C(e) is even and r(e)=C(e)/2 is the exact directional cut demand. For a schedule sigma, actual incident workload equals mandatory vertex load plus edge-use slack. On a star with a fixed center, m' moved leaves and q nontrivial leaf cycles, OPT=m'+q.
assumptions: The graph is a finite undirected tree.
There is exactly one distinct token at every vertex and destinations form a permutation.
Every parallel round is a matching and swaps tokens on all selected edges.
For the exact star formula, the center token is fixed and the leaf target permutation fixes the remaining leaves.
The Bansal-Gunluk-Shapley comparison concerns their uncolored parallel token-swapping model and their d_max lower bound.
verified_steps: For every edge cut, the number of tokens leaving one side equals the number entering it because the destination map is bijective.
Therefore C(e)=2r(e), where r(e) is an integer exact directional crossing demand.
For every schedule, the number of swaps on e is at least r(e); defining Delta_sigma(e)=s_sigma(e)-r(e) yields exact vertex workload decomposition.
A matching permits at most one incident swap per vertex per round, giving the vertex-load lower bound together with the token-distance lower bound.
For a fixed-center star, any schedule is a word of star transpositions because at most one star edge can be used per round.
The cycle-count argument proves the exact fixed-center star value m'+q, including arbitrary extra swaps on fixed leaves.
The ratio on this family is at most 3/2 relative to LB_hub, so it is not an unbounded separation.

The Bansal-Gunluk-Shapley primary paper explicitly gives Theta(h) d_max stretch on subdivided stars and uses a fixed-center star lower-bound instance, so the high-degree phenomenon is known prior art.
gaps: No universal constant alpha with OPT<=alpha*LB_hub was proved.
No parameterized family with OPT/LB_hub tending to infinity was constructed.
A branch-flow cycle count has not been proved to be a valid lower bound in general trees with multiple tokens per branch.
No token-preserving exchange-ordering lemma converts static edge slots into a schedule on arbitrary trees.
No polynomial-time constructive schedule relative to LB_hub was established.
uncertainty: The cut-parity and workload-decomposition lemmas are complete under the stated permutation model.
The exact multi-cycle star formula is complete, but its bounded 3/2 ratio does not decide arbitrary-tree LB_hub stretch.
The branch-flow dependency certificate and token-preserving exchange-ordering lemma remain open.
The source audit establishes the subdivided-star novelty boundary for the claims used here, not a global absence theorem through every venue.

counterexamples.name: multi_cycle_fixed_center_star
counterexamples.scope: The ratio is at most 3/2; this does not refute bounded LB_hub stretch.

checks: Cut balance was derived from the bijective destination map rather than assumed from path symmetry.
The workload decomposition distinguishes actual edge uses from unavoidable directional demand.
The star formula was checked by cycle-count changes under star transpositions and by a matching upper construction.
The finite star extension was not promoted to an arbitrary-tree approximation theorem.
The published subdivided-star stretch result was treated as a novelty boundary, not as supporting evidence for a new claim.
independent_review.scope_limit: The review validates the structural lemmas and the bounded star obstruction; it does not validate a general-tree scheduling theorem.

fully_proved: C(e) is even and r(e)=C(e)/2 is exact directional demand
mandatory vertex load plus edge-use slack decomposition
independently_reproduced: previous fixed-center cyclic star result remains unchanged and is recovered at q=1
all new arithmetic follows directly from the definitions and the star-transposition cycle count
known_prior_art: Theta(h) maximum-distance stretch on subdivided stars
plausible_but_unproved: a constant-factor upper bound relative to LB_hub
a valid branch-flow dependency certificate for arbitrary trees
disproved: LB_hub is exact on every tree
the star high-degree bottleneck is a new phenomenon

literature_audit.source: Bansal, Gunluk, Shapley, Parallel Token Swapping for Qubit Routing, arXiv v2 2025
literature_audit.finding: Theorem 5(c) gives Theta(h) stretch of d_max on subdivided stars, with a fixed-center star lower-bound instance; Theorem 3 gives a polynomial 4OPT+min{OPT,h}+1 bound on subdivided stars.

literature_audit.source: Aichholzer et al., Hardness of Token Swapping on Trees, ESA 2022
literature_audit.finding: Defines parallel rounds as matching swaps and proves NP-hardness on trees, including subdivided stars.

literature_audit.source: Alon, Chung, Graham, Routing Permutations on Graphs via Matchings, 1994
literature_audit.finding: Provides the matching-routing model; its worst-case routing-number results do not imply an instance-sensitive LB_hub theorem.

literature_audit.source: Zhang, Optimal Bounds for Matching Routing on Trees, 1999
literature_audit.finding: Proves a worst-case 3n/2+O(log n) routing bound on trees, not a bound in terms of the instance-specific LB_hub.

next_falsifiable_action: Define a branch-flow dependency certificate at one vertex and prove or refute its lower-bound validity on an overlapping-hub tree; then state the exact token-preserving exchange-ordering lemma required for any LB_hub-relative schedule.
observed_result_or_blocker: Partial mathematical progress is verified, but the core arbitrary-tree constant-stretch objective is unresolved; strict proof-obligation validation therefore classifies this artifact as incomplete rather than scientifically completed.
